title: Mwaghavul language - Wikipedia
text: Afro-Asiatic language.Mwaghavul (also known as Sura) is an Afro-Asiatic language spoken in Plateau State in central Nigeria and predominantly in Mangu LGA.[2]. Mwaghavul's dialects include Takas.[3] The Mupun people is a related ethnic group.

title: Mwaghavul Web
text: Mwaghavul is an Afro-Asiatic language spoken in Plateau State, dominantly in Mangu L.G.A., Middle Belt Region of Nigeria. They are made up nine Districts namely: Mangu, Kombun, Kerang, Ampang, Mangun, Chakfem, Jipal, Panyam and Pushit.

text: Mwaghavul is a stable indigenous language of Nigeria. It belongs to the Afro-Asiatic language family. Direct evidence is lacking, but the language is thought to be used as a first language by all in the ethnic community.

text: Located in the North-Central East of Nigeria, Mwaghavul is one of the 150 Chadic languages belonging to the Afro-Asiatic phylla. The Chadic family is divided into 4 major branches: West, Central, East, and West.
